newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures end mixed, then ease on AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures end mixed, then ease on AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Wednesday in a moderate session, then eased slightly on ACCESS after the weekly AGA gas stock report showed a greater-than-expected build, industry sources said.
December gained one cent to close at $2.684 per million British thermal units, then slipped to $2.655 on ACCESS. January settled 2.8 cents higher at $2.678. Others ended mixed.
"The (AGA) number was on the high end of expectations. It's a little negative," said one East Coast trader, adding cash and futures firmed early Wednesday on forecasts for colder weekend weather.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 27 bcf to 86 percent of capacity, with eastern inventories gaining 22 bcf to 96 percent full. Overall stocks are still 233 bcf, or eight percent, below year-ago. A Reuter poll earlier showed most expected a build in the 15-25 bcf range. Traders said revised forecasts calling for below-normal Midwest and Eastern temperatures later this week and next may provide some support to paper and physical markets.
Technically, traders still pegged December support in the low-$2.50s, with resistance seen at today's high of $2.745 and then at the $2.88 contract high.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices gained almost a dime Wednesday to about the $2.70 level. Midwest prices were up a similar amount to the high-$2.50s. Forecasts for colder weekend weather firmed New York city gate gas prices by several cents to the mid-$2.90s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 0.4 cent to $2.181. NYMEX said 36,785 Hub contracts traded, up from Tuesday's revised tally of 35,060.
NYMEX December Alberta natgas closed 2.5 cents higher at a new contract high of $1.255, while deferreds were untraded. NYMEX said five Alberta contracts traded, even with Tuesday.
NYMEX December Permian natgas ended up five cents at $2.51, while deferreds settled two to four cents higher. NYMEX said 51 lots changed hands versus no trading on Tuesday.

On the KCBT, December finished 0.7 cent higher at $2.52, while deferreds settled up by two to 45 cents. The December East/West spread widened by 0.3 cent to 16.4 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 242 contracts traded, up from Tuesday's total of 158.
